title: Getting out (and saving)
summary: Save, quit, force-quit, and every panic fix for 'I am stuck in vim'.

steps.title: Save and quit
body: All of these are typed in **normal mode** (press `Esc` first). Ex commands start with `:` and run with **Enter**.
| `:q` | quit; **refuses** if there are unsaved changes |
| `:wq` or `:x` | write and quit (`:x` only writes if something changed) |
| `ZZ` | same as `:x`, no colon, no Enter |
| `:w newname.conf` | save a copy under another name |
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: You are in insert mode in a changed file. Order the keys to save and quit.
steps.explain: Esc leaves insert mode; `:wq` then Enter runs write-and-quit.

steps.prompt: You typed `:q` and vim says `E37: No write since last change (add ! to override)`. You want to keep the file as it was on disk. What now?
steps.explain: `!` forces the quit and discards the edits. `:wq` would save the mess you wanted to throw away.

steps.prompt: Match the command to its effect.
pairs: write the buffer to another file

steps.title: The panic kit
body: "I'm stuck in vim" is almost always one of these:
1. **Keys type into the file.** You are in insert mode. Press `Esc`.
2. **You typed `:q` and see your text, but nothing happens.** You are still in insert mode, so `:q` went into the file. `Esc`, `u` to undo it, then `:q!`.
3. **The screen froze.** You pressed `Ctrl+S` (terminal flow control stops output). Press `Ctrl+Q`.

4. **`E325: ATTENTION` / `Found a swap file`.** Another vim has this file open, or a previous session crashed. Read the message: `O` opens read-only, `R` recovers, `D` deletes the swap file (only if you are sure nothing else is editing), `Q` quits.
5. **A window called `[Command Line]` appeared.** You typed `q:`. Type `:q` to close it.
6. **`Recording @q` at the bottom.** You pressed `q` then a letter; press `q` again to stop recording.

steps.prompt: Match the symptom to the fix.
pairs: Every key you press appears in the file
The terminal stopped responding after Ctrl+S

steps.prompt: You are in insert mode on an empty file and, trying to quit, you type `:wq` and press Enter, then `Esc`. What does the file contain now (unsaved)?
steps.explain: In insert mode `:wq` is just text, and Enter starts a new, empty second line. That is why the panic kit says: Esc first, then `u`.

steps.title: What does the command do?
prompt: Model how vim answers a quit command. Write `string Outcome(string command, bool modified)`:
Leading and trailing spaces in `command` are ignored.
template: Dojo.Eq(":q on a clean file", "quit", Outcome(":q", false));
Dojo.Eq(":q on a modified file", "E37", Outcome(":q", true));
Dojo.Eq("ZQ on a clean file", "quit", Outcome("ZQ", false));
Dojo.Eq(":wq always writes", "saved, quit", Outcome(":wq", false));
Dojo.Eq("ZZ skips writing a clean file", "quit", Outcome("ZZ", false));
Dojo.Eq(":x writes a modified file", "saved, quit", Outcome(" :x ", true));
